To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the role of collocation in the assessment of L2 oral production is dependent upon the task, the language of the raters, and the type of analysis.

(1) the use of collocations in L2 oral production is positively associated with the L2 oral proficiency of learners, (2) the association between collocations and L2 oral proficiency is stronger when the raters of the proficiency are the learners’ L2 teachers, (3) the association between L2 oral proficiency and collocation use is stronger when we use cross-sectional data, and (4) the association between oral proficiency and collocations is stronger when the learners have more experience with
the use of collocations in L2 speaking is related to the L2 proficiency of the speakers and the use of collocational knowledge is an important component of L2 oral production.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of L1 in L2 acquisition.
the role of collocation in the development and assessment of L2 oral performance.
a particular type of lexical cohesion in spoken discourse, collocations, and the way in which collocations may be related to the oral proficiency of second language learners.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
collocation plays a primary role not only in determining various dimensions in oral proficiency, but also in L2 oral development.
the role of collocation use in L2 oral production is still unclear and that the findings of this study should be considered as a starting point to further research on the topic.
collocation is a crucial component in L2 oral performance and that the role of collocation in the assessment and development of L2 oral skills should be taken into account.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of collocation is an important factor in the assessment of oral proficiency, but that the relationship between collocation and proficiency is complex.
the role of collocation is not only to be considered as a linguistic feature of oral proficiency, but as a feature of oral proficiency development, as well.
collocation is a key feature of spoken L2 proficiency and development.
The main takeaway from our work is that

collocation use is a strong predictor of L2 oral fluency and comprehensibility, and a moderate predictor of L2 lexical richness, but it is not a strong predictor of lexical accuracy or complexity, and it does not predict lexical diversity.
the collocation-based approach to assessing L2 oral proficiency can provide a more comprehensive and reliable measure than the more conventional approaches.
the collocation effect is robust and consistent across tasks and rater languages.
